subject: English
passage:
Text 1
In earlier decades, feature films were distributed on physical reels that had to be shipped to theaters and changed during screenings. Each reel could hold only about twenty minutes of footage, and theaters could manage just a limited number of reels per showing. This pushed directors and editors to trim their films carefully and cut anything that wasn't essential. Filmmakers today face far fewer restrictions on runtime because digital distribution has replaced physical reels. As a result, many films being released now are noticeably longer than films from past decades.

Text 2
In the current era of streaming, most feature films are distributed digitally rather than on physical reels. Digital platforms impose almost no technical limit on how long a movie can be. This is likely why many recently released films run longer and contain more scenes than films made for earlier distribution methods. Unfortunately, a number of these longer films feel padded and lose momentum in the middle.
prompt: Based on the texts, the author of Text 1 and the author of Text 2 would most likely agree with which statement about many new films?

choices.A: Many new films use more visual effects than films generally once used.
choices.B: Many new films earn more at the box office than films generally once earned.
choices.C: Many new films are longer than films generally once were.
choices.D: Many new films contain less dialogue than films generally once contained.

explanation:
Choice C is the best answer. Both texts agree that many new films are longer than films from the past. Text 1 states that 'many films being released now are noticeably longer than films from past decades,' and Text 2 states that 'many recently released films run longer and contain more scenes than films made for earlier distribution methods.' Although the texts differ in whether they treat this trend neutrally or negatively, both authors clearly acknowledge that modern films tend to be longer.

Why B is incorrect:

Choice B is incorrect. Neither text discusses box office earnings or how much money new films make compared to older films, so there is no evidence that either author would agree with this statement.
